issues.problem:
A hidden part steers the mass and balance shown. This is a regression against f7ac37d since round 2, and round 3 keeps it. Reviewer V1 found it at 19:21; the restarted V2 instance reproduced it (scratch shift-v2-3/out/hmass2.txt, hmass3.txt); I confirmed the mechanism in the code.

The mechanism: MassProps.ownership orders every part kept first, then by slot rank, then by Sampling.measureRanked. acrossTies tests `kept[q.index] == kept[p.index]`, which is also true between two cleaned parts. So a cleaned part is placed from the centre of the cleaned parts it ties with on volume and height, and another hidden part moves that centre.

Editor-only construction:
- Start from F2. Add a sealed Iron box on its blade's top: parts 11-16, walls 0.02 thick, 0.3 across, centre y 4.1.
- Fill the box with two hidden fillers 0.18 x 0.26 x 0.26 that overlap 0.1 along X: 17 Iron at x -0.04 and 18 Steel at x +0.04. Both are Enclosed.
- Ctrl+D filler 18 in place (19, an exact copy, Enclosed).

Live (and round 2):
- Without 19, part 17 owns the overlap (17: 0.012168, 18: 0.005408), mass 1.29371984, balance 0.387402095.
- With 19, part 18 owns it (17: 0.005408, 18: 0.012168), mass 1.29358464 (-0.000135), balance 0.387165618 (-0.000236).
- G is the same (Smelting 0.0928, Hammering 0.4204, Sharpening 0.1939). With the materials swapped, the effect reverses.

f7ac37d: the copy changes nothing (mass 1.29106654 or 1.29092458 either way).

It makes these SPEC statements false:
- §4.4: cleaned parts 'never count for ... another part's place in either rank (... the measure's ties kept parts alone) ... so a hidden part steers none of the physics a player is shown (balance, ...)'.
- §4.5: 'no hidden part moves the balance ... S4 shows'.
- §17.2: 'No hidden part moves another part's place in either rank'.
- §4.3: ownership 'among the kept parts it ties with'.
issues.fix:
Tried by the restarted instance in this folder (shift-v2-3/out/fix_cleaned_noplace.diff, tree var/hfix0). In acrossTies a cleaned part gets no place, and a kept part's centre is taken over kept parts only:

```
local qx, qz = 0, 0
if kept[p.index] then
	local sx, sz, n = 0, 0, 0
	for j = 1, N do
		local q = parts[j]
		local kq = keys[q.index]
		if kq[1] == kp[1] and kq[2] == kp[2] and kept[q.index] then
			sx += q.cx
			sz += q.cz
			n += 1
		end
	end
	qx, qz = place(p.cx - sx / n), place(p.cz - sz / n)
end
kp[3], kp[4], kp[5], kp[6] = abs(qx), qx, abs(qz), qz
```

Between tied hidden parts the material decides, then the index; an overlap split between two parts of one material moves no mass. Results:
- The pin below passes.
- The tree reads live byte for byte on the 136 fixtures, Parity's 200, the six seed streams and all 33,389 plausible designs.
- --quick: 731 pass.
- Neither the copy nor a whole-design move of 0.05 changes the probe.

Alternative (out/fix_cleaned_places.diff): cleaned parts placed from the world's planes. It is equally hidden-proof and reads live on every corpus, but a 0.05 move along the fillers' axis swaps their shares (mass -0.000135), as on f7ac37d.

Pin (out/pin_hidden_ownership.diff), Invariance.spec 'T-DIF-04 a hidden part steers no ownership among hidden parts': the construction above, asserting every owned volume, the mass, the balance and the steps. It fails on live ('owned volume 11: expected 0.012168, got 0.005408') and passes on both repairs and on f7ac37d's source.

Then correct the four SPEC sentences, for example §4.4: 'a cleaned part has no place in the measure's rank, so no hidden part moves another's'.
